sentences.text: Archaeornithura possessed feathers with a central groove, a feature linked to advanced flight capabilities, alongside a thighbone that was notably short compared to its tarsometatarsus.
This species represents the oldest known member of the ornithuromorph lineage, the group containing all modern birds and their extinct relatives.
Two fossil specimens were unearthed in the Huajiying Formation in Hebei Province, China, marking the first ornithuromorph fossil found in this geological layer.

An international team led by Wang and Zhou Zhonge from the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology in Beijing named and described the species, announcing their findings in Nature Communications in May 2015.
Evidence suggests Archaeornithura was adept at flying.
Researchers Zhou and Wang hypothesize that these avian traits may have helped ornithuromorphs survive the Cretaceous-Paleogene mass extinction.
Archaeornithura is classified within the family Hongshanornithidae and was identified as the sister taxon of Tianyuornis through phylogenetic analysis.
The animal lived during the Hauterivian age approximately 130.7 million years ago, with a broader estimated time range spanning from 132.6 to 125.77 million years ago.
